lesson: Only automate a task that is both repetitive and annoying. If it is not annoying, let your people keep doing it.
detail: AI will not get good at non-repetitive work, and non-annoying work is what people actually want to do.

lesson: Three percent margin turned over twelve billing cycles is a thirty percent return on capital. Pitch against that, not the margin.
detail: On a $100M project with about $15M of working capital, productivity software aimed at the 3 percent is aimed at the wrong economics.

lesson: An owner who can explain exactly what changed after a fatality may be safer than a contractor with a clean record.
detail: No single prequalification data point should disqualify. A risk signal should trigger a conversation about what the company learned.

lesson: Distrust any vendor claim of hours saved per week. Those are hours 41 to 50, not the hours that matter.
detail: With two to four year project lifespans, real pilot metrics take years, and vendors who oversell to get in the door guarantee disappointment on the job.

lesson: Never burn a bridge in commercial construction. You will work with the same people again wearing different hard hats.
detail: Houston is the fourth-largest city in the country and a small world. Crews and managers cross paths across projects and companies for decades.

lesson: Missed submittal dates are the earliest reliable warning of schedule delay. Track them before you track anything else.
detail: Submittal adherence is the single best leading indicator, but one-by-one workflows push teams to Excel, which destroys the indicator's reliability.

lesson: Do not automate the tasks that train your people. The PE walking the site with a camera is learning the job.
detail: Mundane tasks build muscle memory. A photo robot removes the development the PE was getting from the walk. Which tasks to protect is a deliberate decision.
role: VP of Digital Solutions, Skanska USA

lesson: Before blaming a worker's choice, prove the work was planned, the equipment was there, and the training and time existed.
detail: Exhaust systemic failures first. Only after convincing yourself of all of those can an individual factor even be considered.

lesson: If you are not doing concrete lift drawings and MEP coordination before a pour, you are leaving risk on a 16-hour activity you cannot undo.
detail: Nothing moves a job faster than a concrete pour, and nothing is harder to fix. Concrete planning is VDC's highest-leverage work on any job.

lesson: Pricing preconstruction too cheap can lose you the job. One owner rejected a GC for exactly that reason.
detail: Owners now read precon as value rather than a free loss leader. Being the cheapest signaled the least effort.

lesson: Running 400 adults at 6am as a dictatorship will fail. People only listen when they are part of the conversation.
detail: Daily coordination of hundreds of workers works because they are treated as participants, not subordinates. Command and control is rewarded culturally but is less effective.

lesson: Hit only 25 percent of critical path milestones for eight straight months and you have forfeited any claim to a time extension.
detail: On a $200M project the contractor kept saying 'we'll be fine' until admitting a month of delay three months from completion. The pattern itself became the owner's case.

lesson: On the owner side you do not call the shots. You ask leading questions until the GC arrives at the solution itself.
detail: The presumption that owners command is a fallacy. Influence, and respect for the GC's means and methods, is how the work gets done.

lesson: An LLM does not know it is wrong and wants to please you, so it will build your confidence on the wrong path.
detail: Confirmation bias instead of course correction: a specific operational hazard for anyone checking their judgment against a chatbot.
role: VP of Digital Solutions, Skanska USA

lesson: If you are doing the innovator's job right, today could be your last day. You cannot protect your job and ask hard questions.
detail: Risk tolerance, including willingness to be fired, belongs in the job description. He applies the diagnosis to the whole industry.
